# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 41 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 41 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_041_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 10 — On Grief

**41:1** "Remove grief from yourself," he said, "for she is the sister of double-mindedness and of bitterness." "How, lord," I said, "is she the sister of these? For to me bitterness and double-mindedness seem different things." "You are foolish, man," he said. "Do you not understand that grief is the most evil of all spirits and most ruinous to the servants of God, and destroys a man more than all the other spirits, and wears out the Holy Spirit, and again saves it?"

**41:2** "I am without understanding, lord," I said, "and I do not comprehend these parables. For how it can wear out and again save, I cannot comprehend." "Listen," he said. "Those who have never made inquiry about the truth nor investigated concerning the Deity, but have simply believed, and have become entangled in business affairs and riches and friendships of the Gentiles and many other concerns of this world — those who have been occupied with these things do not comprehend the parables of divinity. For they are darkened by these concerns and corrupted and made barren."

**41:3** "But those who fear God and inquire concerning divinity and truth and direct their hearts toward the Lord, to them all things are easily grasped and they understand everything said to them, because the fear of the Lord is in them. For where the Lord dwells, there also is great understanding. Cleave therefore to the Lord, and you shall understand and perceive all things."

**41:4** "Listen now, senseless one, how grief wears out the Holy Spirit, and how it saves. When the double-minded man undertakes any deed and fails in it on account of his double-mindedness, grief enters into the man and grieves the Holy Spirit and wears it out."

**41:5** "Then again, when bitterness cleaves to a man and he is grieved about some matter — about a transaction, or about food, or about some foolish word that was spoken, or about some friend, or about a giving or receiving, or about certain other such foolish things — grief enters into the heart of the man who has been made bitter, and he is troubled and the Holy Spirit is grieved."

**41:6** "Again, anger, when it comes upon a man in some matter, and he is made bitter — and again on account of these same things grief enters and makes the heart of the man sad. So it wears out the Holy Spirit. But again it saves — hear in what way it saves: when a sinner perceives his sins and repents, grief comes upon him as his salvation. Now this grief over sins saves. Both griefs then are found together: the grief that saves and the grief that destroys."

**41:7** "Clothe yourself therefore with cheerfulness, which always has favor before God and is acceptable to him, and rejoice in it. For every cheerful man does good things and thinks good things and despises grief. But the sorrowful man always does evil — first, because he grieves the Holy Spirit, which was given to man for joy; and second, because by grieving the Holy Spirit he works lawlessness, neither praying to God nor giving thanks to him. Therefore the prayer of the sorrowful man has no power to ascend to the altar of God."

**41:8** "Because why?" I said. "Because grief sits in his heart," he said. "Grief mixed with prayer does not allow the prayer to ascend in purity to the altar. For as wine mixed with vinegar no longer has the same pleasant taste, so also grief mixed with the Holy Spirit does not have the same intercession. Therefore cleanse yourself from this evil grief and you shall live to God; and all shall live to God who cast away grief from themselves and clothe themselves with all cheerfulness."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the personification of grief and the paratactic style of Hermas.*
